content.comment_body: For Q1 and Q2 of [product_name] 2020, I measure 24 volts. Shouldn't they be fully disconnected when there is no configuration in the signal definition and they're reported as off in monitoring on the web interface?

The outputs on the [product_name] are transistor type. Most likely, you're seeing 24VDC because digital meters with high internal resistance pick that up. With an older analog meter, you'd probably see no voltage. Also, are the output control LEDs off?
Hi, yes, the LEDs are off.

There are differences between modules: some [product_name] base modules use relay outputs and others use transistor outputs. With relay outputs, you can actually measure something since the contacts are potential-free.
Okay, I think I understand now. I should have read the manual. Thank you for your help. You probably saved my [product_name]. I connected an LED to it and it lights up.
Just a note: it's better to add a new post instead of editing your previous one once someone has replied.
Sorry about the editing. The LEDs remain off, but devices connected to the outputs are on. I only configured input 1 and 2 for messaging.
The outputs support a maximum of 300 mA and are non-isolated. Incorrect wiring or excessive load could have damaged them.
Nothing was connected to the outputs until now; currently it's just a 2 mA LED.

Sorry, I meant 200 mA. Nevertheless, the current is very low. It wasn't functioning previously, unless you're suggesting that measuring with the meter may have damaged it. Is it possible I'm misprogramming it or the unit was faulty from the start?

You mentioned only configuring the inputs to trigger a text message, not the outputs. Why did you wire some outputs? Maybe the 2mA load is too small. Please clarify each step you're taking, so we can follow.
Did you connect the LEDs directly, maybe without a resistor?

No major update—just explaining that everything else works; text from inputs 1 and 2 is successful. The only issue is I can't switch off outputs Q1 and Q2. I swapped the meter for a LED while messaging. Still unable to turn off Q1 and Q2.
I'm sorry, but 'nothing new' doesn't answer my previous questions. Please provide a drawing of your LED connection and let us know the LED specifications.
Hello, why do you want to close the topic if you haven't found a solution yet?

analysis.insight_summary: The user is unsure about the expected behavior of [product_name] outputs, in particular whether they should display 24V or be fully disconnected when not configured. The technical details of transistor versus relay outputs are not obvious from the monitoring interface or documentation. There is a mismatch between visual status indicators and actual output measurements, causing confusion and concerns about whether the device is damaged or defective.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects outputs to be fully disconnected and show no voltage when switched off, both in the interface and in real-world operation.
